title: Degreewise ordinary base tensor comparison
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, A and B commutative R-algebras, and M an A-module. Use the tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change]. There exists a B-linear isomorphism B ⊗_R Res_R M ≅ Res_B ((A ⊗_R B) ⊗_A M) which sends b ⊗ m to (1 ⊗ b) ⊗ m for every b and m. Ring and module universes may differ with carriers in a common containing universe. No flatness is assumed.

proof.text: Define the B-linear forward map b ⊗ m ↦ (1 ⊗ b) ⊗ m and inverse (a ⊗ b) ⊗ m ↦ b ⊗ am using the tensor universal property. R-balancing uses the algebra structures; A-balancing uses (aa₀)m = a(a₀m).

The composites fix pure tensors: one returns b ⊗ m, and the other returns (1 ⊗ b) ⊗ am = (a ⊗ b) ⊗ m by A-balancing. Tensor induction proves both identities, giving the isomorphism and generator formula. Mathlib IsPushout.cancelBaseChange and cancelBaseChange_symm_tmul implement this after transport of the scalar actions.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_baseTensorOrdinaryDegreeIso
    (R : Type uR) (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (M : ModuleCat.{max uR uA uB v} A) :
    ∃ e :
      (extendScalars.{_, _, max uR uA uB v} (algebraMap R B)).obj
        ((restrictScalars.{max uR uA uB v} (algebraMap R A)).obj M) ≅
      (restrictScalars.{max uR uA uB v}
        Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom).obj
        ((extendScalars.{_, _, max uR uA uB v}
          (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B))).obj M),
      ∀ (b : B) (m : M), e.hom (b ⊗ₜ[R,algebraMap R B] m) =
        Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight b ⊗ₜ[A,algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B)] m
